G2.evidence: Texas does not publish a disciplinary register we can query.

G3.evidence: No matching entity on the Texas list of active franchise taxpayers. Texas does not require a sole proprietorship or a general partnership to pay franchise tax, and an exempt entity is left off as well, so this is a check this source cannot complete rather than evidence against the firm. The state's own SOSDirect service can settle it for a fee

faq.q: How much does The Injury Law Guides charge?
faq.a: The Injury Law Guides publishes no fee terms on the pages we read, so none is recorded on this profile. An absence here is not a claim that the firm has no fee arrangement, only that it does not state one publicly. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does The Injury Law Guides offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. The Injury Law Guides publishes a free initial consultation. It publishes material in Spanish.

faq.q: Where does The Injury Law Guides have offices?
faq.a: The Injury Law Guides publishes one office, in San Antonio. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at The Injury Law Guides?
faq.a: The Injury Law Guides names five attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: Texas does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.q: Are the case results The Injury Law Guides publishes verified?
faq.a: No. The Injury Law Guides publishes 54 case results with amounts on its own site. We counted them and we did not confirm them: the figures are the firm's. Pillar B scores whether a firm publishes outcomes and discloses them properly, including whether a prior-results disclaimer appears beside them, not whether the amounts are right. Past results do not predict another case.

faq.q: What has Law Firm Listings verified about The Injury Law Guides?
faq.a: The Injury Law Guides scores 56 and sits at Verified. Passed: website and footprint. Did not pass: entity registration. Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure and discipline. Every row of the scorecard above names where the value came from and when it was read. Nothing on this profile was supplied by the firm for payment, and no placement here can be bought.
